output.brief: The rejections were caused by the cooperative's own paperwork, not by the fungicide, the growers, or Meridane's equipment. When Tallis was introduced, the Meridane mandarin product record was copied from an avocado record and carries a 7.0°C carriage setpoint, while mandarins need 4.0°C. Every rejected container was a Meridane container set at 7°C; the Meridane containers at 4°C (K1) and all Coastway containers passed. The units held their setpoints within 0.4°C, and K3 was rejected on the old fungicide, so the fungicide does not explain it. Confidence is high on the mechanism, though I did not check rainfall or the grower diaries. Next: correct PRD-MAND-01 to 4.0°C now, ask Meridane to reset the containers at sea and queued (sailing 3 Oct and 10 Oct), and add a check comparing reefer settings to the product specification. Hold the grower suspension, the Meridane cargo claim, and the Brindle deduction until the record is reviewed. Use independent loggers on the next sailings to confirm.
